title: Family, people and celebrations (Feste und Familie)
summary: Talk about your wider family and the people around you, congratulate someone, and accept an invitation.
goals: Name more family members: Großeltern, Ehemann, Ehefrau, Partner
Talk about people: Leute, Mensch, Junge, Mädchen

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 15: Family (Meine Familie, Meine Eltern)

sections.title: People
sections.text:
- [[die Leute]] = people, always plural: [[Die Leute hier sind nett.]]
- [[der Mensch]] = a person, a human being: [[Hier wohnen viele Menschen.]]
- [[das Mädchen]] is neuter because of -chen (Unit 2): [[Das Mädchen heißt Eva.]]
- [[mein Mann]] and [[meine Frau]] (Unit 2) are the everyday words for husband and wife. [[Ehemann]] and [[Ehefrau]] are what forms say.

sections.title: Congratulations and good wishes
sections.text:
- [[Herzlichen Glückwunsch!]] = Congratulations! For a birthday, a wedding, a new job. Learn it as one block; the -en ending comes at A2 (Unit 14).
- [[Herzlichen Glückwunsch zum Geburtstag!]] or [[Alles Gute zum Geburtstag!]] (Unit 3)
- [[Ich gratuliere dir!]] [[gratulieren]] takes the dative (Unit 6).
- [[Viel Glück!]] = Good luck!
- [[Herzlich willkommen!]] = A warm welcome!
- [[Wir heiraten im Juni.]] [[Die Hochzeit ist am zwölften Juni.]]
- [[Danke für die Einladung! Ich komme gern.]]
Russian поздравляю тебя takes the accusative (тебя). German [[gratulieren]] takes the dative: [[Ich gratuliere dir.]], not 'dich'.

sections.title: When you're invited
sections.text: Invited to someone's home? Bring something small, like flowers ([[Blumen]]) or a drink, and be on time ([[pünktlich]], Unit 3). For a party, a little late is fine.

items.de: Danke für die Einladung! Ich komme gern.
items.en: Thanks for the invitation! I'd love to come.

items.de: Das Fest war super. Wir haben viel gelacht.
items.en: The party was great. We laughed a lot.

items.question: Your colleague just got married. What do you say?
items.explanation: Herzlichen Glückwunsch! for good news. Gute Besserung! is for someone who's ill.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: Happy birthday! (I congratulate you)
Fill in the gap: Thanks for the invitation!

items.question: Which article goes with Mädchen?
items.explanation: -chen is always das, even for a girl: das Mädchen.
